sections.name: Hook
lines: q_hook
You can rip a chunk off a QR code, and it still works. Here's the trick.
q_title
It's all hidden in plain sight, in five steps.

sections.name: Finding the code
lines: q_finders
Step one. Those three big squares in the corners tell your camera where the code is, and which way up it's sitting.
q_timing
Thin dotted lines between them act like a ruler, so the camera knows how big each little square is.
q_align
And a smaller square near the fourth corner helps straighten out a code seen at an angle.

sections.name: Ones and zeros
lines: q_bits
Step two. Every little square is a bit. Dark means one. Light means zero.
q_bytes
Read in a set zigzag order, groups of eight bits become letters, numbers, or a web address.
q_format
A few squares by the corners aren't data at all. They describe how the rest of the code is laid out.

sections.name: Spare copies
lines: q_errors
Step three. Part of the code is extra data, a kind of mathematical backup, called error correction.
q_torn
At the highest setting, up to about thirty percent of the code can be scratched, torn or covered, and it still scans.
q_logo
That's why brands can stick a logo right in the middle.

sections.name: The mask
lines: q_mask
Step four. Big blocks of one colour would confuse the scanner. So the pattern is shuffled with one of eight masks, and the code notes which one it used.
q_unmask
Your phone simply undoes the mask before reading the bits.

sections.name: Size and safety
lines: q_sizes
Step five. Codes come in forty sizes, from twenty-one squares across, up to a hundred and seventy-seven, holding thousands of characters.
q_safe
Your camera decodes one in a split second. But a QR code can point anywhere, so check the link before you tap.
q_origin
Not bad for an idea from 1994, invented to track car parts in a Japanese factory.

sections.name: Recap
lines: w_recap
Corners find the code. Every square is a bit. Backup data fixes the damage, and a mask keeps it readable.
outro
Next time you scan one, you'll know you're reading a grid of ones and zeros. Follow for more of the tech you use every day.
